chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from 'Isa ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the aged animal whose teeth have fallen out, that there is no problem with it regarding the sacrificial animals; and if you bought it as thin and found it as fat, it would suffice you; and if you bought it as thin and found it as thin, then it would not suffice.
And in another report, 'The limit of thinness is when there is not anything of fat upon its kidneys.'

key_terms.أَجْزَأَكَ: It suffices you (is valid for the obligation)
key_terms.الْهَرِمِ: The aged animal (specifically one whose teeth have fallen out)

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for a sacrificial animal to be valid if it is thin or aged?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the juristic distinction between natural aging (herm) and pathological wasting (huzl), establishing that the latter invalidates the sacrifice only if the fat reserves on the kidneys are entirely depleted. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on practical inspection (tashkhis) to ensure the animal's fitness for worship, balancing textual criteria with observable physical conditions. This ruling underscores the principle that defects must be significant enough to detract from the animal's value and suitability for offering.
